ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives a stepped rectangular output waveform with a period of 2π. In the positive half-cycle of the waveform there is a positive pulse with amplitude +1, and α is used in the figure to mark the width of this positive pulse; at a position separated by π there is a negative pulse with amplitude -1, whose shape corresponds to the positive pulse, reflecting half-wave symmetry. The output in the remaining intervals is 0. Reasoning: Model this output as a half-wave symmetric rectangular pulse waveform according to the figure. For this kind of waveform, the amplitude factor of the nth nonzero odd harmonic is proportional to sin(nα/2). To make the output contain no 5th harmonic, the 5th harmonic factor should be set to zero: sin(5α/2)=0. Therefore 5α/2=mπ, giving α=2mπ/5. Taking the first actual nonzero solution m=1, then α=2π/5=72°.

raw_record.question_text: With reference to the output waveform shown in the image, at what value of \(\alpha\) will the output of the converter be free from the 5th harmonic?

method.method_draft: Identify from the image that α denotes the width of the positive output pulse at level +1, with an equal negative pulse at level −1 shifted by π. Model one period as a half-wave symmetric rectangular pulse waveform. Write the nth harmonic coefficient, whose nonzero odd-harmonic magnitude is proportional to sin(nα/2). Set the 5th-harmonic factor to zero: sin(5α/2)=0. Taking the first practical nonzero solution gives α=2π/5=72°.
